subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a narrow bug fix; it creates durable agents, workspaces, configs, skills, memory namespaces, and message-routing authority from group-chat senders.

options.title: Design generic contract first
options.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel owner surface.

options.title: Keep session-only routing
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope and explicit subagent/thread mechanisms, documenting that full per-user agent orchestration belongs in an external plugin or deployment pattern for now.

options.title: Reject automatic provisioning
options.body: Close this feature if maintainers decide group identities should never create durable OpenClaw agents automatically.

recommendation.title: Design generic contract first
recommendation.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel owner surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the freshest checked-in Feishu routing, dynamic-agent, subagent-hook, and docs changes relevant to choosing the permanent shape.
